1.pericope_label: Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks: for that thy name is near thy wondrous works declare

debates.q: What is received in the second verse — a congregation or a set time?

sides.view: A set time: when I have chosen my time, I will judge uprightly
Three senses are possible, but the congregation is meant — the church of the firstborn
The congregation of Israel, restored from captivity

debates.q: What are the pillars the speaker bears up?

sides.view: The mountains, adjusted to the weight they must bear
The divine power on which all things depend
Good magistrates, ministers and men, who are the pillars of a nation
Nothing structural — the verse describes the melting of the earth at the last day

outliers.view: Offers a political reading in which the psalm is spoken before David’s accession, and the pillars of the state are the chief people’s expectation of him, all that keeps them from open rebellion

4.pericope_label: I said unto the fools, Deal not foolishly: and to the wicked, Lift not up the horn

debates.q: What lies behind the horn and the stiff neck?

sides.view: Horned animals — the horn a symbol of honour and strength, the neck wantonly raised
Untamed oxen that will not bow to the yoke
A literal horned diadem, worn erect, as travellers report of Abyssinian kings
The little horn and the ten-horned beast of prophecy

debates.q: How should the unfinished sixth verse be completed?

sides.view: By the received punctuation; Ewald’s four-point reconstruction expects more geographical accuracy than Hebrew poetry offers
By history — no quarter of the compass sent help to Babylon
It may be the boast of the fools, that no exaltation will come from anywhere

outliers.view: Cites a traveller’s report of the horned diadems of Abyssinian kings as evidence for the antiquity of the image behind the stiff neck

7.pericope_label: But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another

debates.q: What is the mixture in the cup?

sides.view: The blending of the portions destined for good and bad in Israel, the dregs left for the rest
Strengthening and intoxicating ingredients, served by God as master of a feast
The stupefying potion given to criminals before execution
Afflictions and judgments measured out in proportion to sins
Christ, who has been speaking throughout the psalm
The psalmist, magnifying God for the promise of deliverance
The poet returning from the foreseen future to his own oppressed present

outliers.view: Assigns the speaking part of the whole psalm to Christ, so that the declaration of the ninth verse is his and its object has to be supplied
Read the words for ever as implying that one who gives himself entirely to the Redeemer does not die at all
